organizations.normalization_notes: The institutional roster's historical combined name is retained; Princeton's finding aid uses Hobart College.
The Marine Corps is retained as a distinct military service, and source wording remains recoverable in each affiliation.

organizations.canonical_name: Unidentified Spokane and San Francisco newspapers
organizations.historical_name: newspapers in Spokane, Wash., and San Francisco, Calif.
organizations.normalization_notes: The Library of Congress finding aid does not name the newspapers. The project does not guess or merge them with known titles.
The historical newspaper title is retained without substituting a successor.
Historical source wording is preserved in each affiliation.
Student status is modeled separately and is not counted as employment.
Participation in an expedition is a professional affiliation, not employment, unless separate evidence establishes employment.

affiliations.research_notes: The HWS roster dates Eddy's presidency through 1942; his Marine Corps service intervened before or alongside the transition to OSS-related work.

affiliations.role_title: commissioned officer and Naval Attaché in Tangier
affiliations.date_precision: year; 1941 start reflects wartime commission material, while Tangier is explicit for 1942
affiliations.research_notes: The finding aid documents the Marine commission, 1942 Tangier assignment, and OSS service, but not the exact administrative boundary between the assignments.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: newspapers in Spokane, Wash., and San Francisco, Calif.
affiliations.research_notes: The finding aid places this employment immediately before Army enlistment but does not identify either newspaper by title.
This specifically named earlier employer is preserved separately from the unnamed 1940-1942 newspaper employers.

affiliations.date_precision: year; assignments in Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia are documented
affiliations.research_notes: The Library of Congress documents Army intelligence service beginning in 1942. Box 243 is still needed to establish the exact OSS administrative sequence.

affiliations.date_precision: month for enrollment; departure year only
affiliations.research_notes: Dartmouth is a documented student affiliation, not an employer and not included in employer analytics.

affiliations.date_precision: year; transfer described as three weeks after an Algeria assignment opportunity
affiliations.research_notes: CIA explicitly describes Hemingway's transfer from his Army Military Police assignment to OSS; the exact transfer date requires Box 326.
The finding aid documents a 1928 Abyssinia expedition for the museum. It does not establish employment, and its National Geographic reference concerns a separate 1952 expedition.
Official history identifies Poole as assisting the branch chief and actually running FN. NARA establishes that the COI branch became part of OSS in June 1942.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Princeton University School of Public Affairs
affiliations.research_notes: Princeton documents Poole's directorship through 1939. The two-year gap before COI prevents labeling it the last civilian employer without further evidence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel William A. Eddy is William Alfred Eddy, the Hobart president and Marine officer documented in Princeton's finding aid.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and initial, colonel rank, wartime Marine service, Tangier assignment, and OSS service align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive exact name plus matching colonel rank and explicit OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Institutional sources document the 1936-1942 presidency and wartime Marine sequence.
claims.match_notes: The Marine evidence corrects the rank-only parser's initial Army classification.

claims.claim_text: Hobart and William Smith Colleges is Eddy's documented last civilian employer before wartime Marine service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The colleges' roster dates his presidency from 1936 through 1942, while Princeton documents his return to Marine service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the exact indexed colonel.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded across the civilian-to-military transition.
claims.match_notes: The college presidency is not mislabeled as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation because military service intervened.

claims.claim_text: Eddy's best-supported immediate wartime affiliation before or alongside his OSS work was his Marine Corps assignment, including 1942 service in Tangier.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Princeton's chronology places a Marine commission and Tangier attaché assignment before its description of his OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the exact indexed colonel.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate pathway; the exact administrative transfer boundary is not stated.
claims.match_notes: The qualified claim does not turn a military assignment into a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Archibald B. Roosevelt is Archibald Bulloch Roosevelt Jr., the Army intelligence officer documented by the Library of Congress.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, captain rank, 1942 Army entry, intelligence training, and North African assignments align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the indexed captain and the Library of Congress intelligence officer share a specific wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The finding aid documents civilian newspaper employment through 1942 followed by Army intelligence service.
claims.match_notes: The suffix omitted from the index is retained as a documented variant rather than silently added to the indexed name.

claims.claim_text: Roosevelt's last documented civilian employment before Army service was with unnamed newspapers in Spokane and San Francisco.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress dates the unnamed newspaper employment to 1940-1942 and Army enlistment to 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Archibald Bulloch Roosevelt Jr.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate before military service, but the newspaper titles are not supplied.
claims.match_notes: No specific Spokane or San Francisco newspaper is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Roosevelt worked for the New York Herald Tribune in 1939.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress biographical chronology names the newspaper and year.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Archibald Bulloch Roosevelt Jr.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, superseded by later newspaper work.
claims.match_notes: This earlier named employer remains separate from the unidentified 1940-1942 newspapers.

claims.claim_text: Roosevelt's best-supported immediate wartime affiliation was United States Army intelligence service in North Africa.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress documents intelligence school and successive Army intelligence assignments beginning in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the indexed captain.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate pathway; Box 243 is needed for the precise OSS sequence.
claims.match_notes: The claim is qualified and does not infer a transfer instrument not yet reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed First Lieutenant John H. Hemingway is John Hadley Nicanor 'Jack' Hemingway, whose Army-to-OSS transfer is documented by CIA.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The expanded full name, indexed initials and rank, officer training, Army assignment, and explicit OSS transfer align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: exact indexed initials plus matching commissioned rank and official transfer chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: CIA documents Dartmouth, Army Military Police, and OSS in sequence.
claims.match_notes: The public profile masks the indexed service number.

claims.claim_text: Hemingway transferred directly to OSS from a United States Army Military Police assignment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA describes his MP unit and states that he was transferred to OSS after accepting hazardous duty.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the indexed first lieutenant.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate transfer, although the page does not supply the exact date.
claims.match_notes: The Army assignment is modeled as military service, not civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: Hemingway enrolled at Dartmouth College in January 1942 and left to enter military service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA explicitly dates the enrollment and describes his departure at age nineteen.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for John Hadley Nicanor Hemingway.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before military and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Dartmouth is presented as student status and excluded from employer counts.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gertrude Legendre is Gertrude Sanford Legendre, whose OSS Message Center service and wartime capture are documented by institutional and NARA records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name, OSS London service, capture chronology, and NARA wartime record listing align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive name plus two independent archival descriptions of OSS-related service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document wartime service and capture but not her immediate pre-OSS status.
claims.match_notes: No commissioned or military status is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Legendre participated in a 1928 Abyssinia expedition for the American Museum of Natural History.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The College of Charleston finding aid identifies the year, location, and museum connection.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Gertrude Sanford Legendre.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar professional affiliation, not shown to be employment or immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: The finding aid's National Geographic expedition is dated 1952 and is excluded from pre-OSS claims.

claims.claim_text: The indexed DeWitt C. Poole is diplomat and educator DeWitt Clinton Poole, who ran COI's Foreign Nationalities Branch.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive full name and initial, Princeton directorship, and official COI branch leadership align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive exact name plus matching academic and predecessor-agency roles.
claims.temporal_assessment: Official sources document the 1941-1942 COI-to-OSS transition.
claims.match_notes: The index has no rank, and the reviewed evidence supports civilian government status rather than a military commission.

claims.claim_text: Poole ran the Foreign Nationalities Branch in COI, the direct predecessor organization redesignated within OSS in June 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA identifies Poole as the official who actually ran FN; NARA documents the branch's COI establishment and OSS transition.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the distinctive indexed person.
claims.match_notes: COI is preserved as a separate historical organization rather than silently collapsed into OSS.

claims.claim_text: Poole served as director of Princeton University's School of Public Affairs from 1933 to 1939.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Princeton's institutional history supplies the role and dates; CIA independently describes him as a former director.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for DeWitt Clinton Poole.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, but not proven to be the last civilian employer before COI.
claims.match_notes: The two-year gap prevents an immediate or last-civilian designation.

research_attempts.query_text: "William A. Eddy" OSS employer Hobart Marines Tangier; NARA, Princeton, HWS, CIA, and military-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar diplomatic and oil-company work was excluded; image-only military references did not establish the pre-OSS employment sequence.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified Hobart as the last civilian employer and qualified the Marine assignment as the best-supported immediate wartime pathway.

research_attempts.query_text: "Archibald B. Roosevelt" OSS Captain employer newspaper Army intelligence; NARA and Library of Congress review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Sources about his father Archibald Roosevelt were rejected; postwar CIA and banking work was excluded; no newspaper title was guessed for 1940-1942.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified named and unnamed newspaper employment and qualified the Army intelligence assignment pending the exact OSS transfer chronology.

research_attempts.query_text: "John H. Hemingway" OSS 1st Lieutenant employer Dartmouth Army Military Police; NARA and CIA official review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar occupations and family-centered biographies were excluded; Dartmouth student status was not converted into employment.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified an explicit Army Military Police-to-OSS transfer and preserved Dartmouth solely as student status.

research_attempts.query_text: "Gertrude Sanford Legendre" OSS employer occupation expedition; NARA and College of Charleston archival review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Socialite labels, family businesses, and Medway ownership did not establish employment; the 1952 National Geographic expedition was postwar and excluded.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified identity and a 1928 museum expedition as a non-employment affiliation; immediate status and employer remain archival questions.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 443 and Mss 0182 wartime files.

research_attempts.query_text: "DeWitt C. Poole" OSS employer Princeton Foreign Nationalities Branch COI; NARA, CIA, Princeton, and contemporary-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar positions were excluded; Princeton was not labeled the last civilian employer because the reviewed record leaves a 1939-1941 gap.
research_attempts.research_notes: Confirmed the COI Foreign Nationalities Branch as the immediate predecessor affiliation and documented, but did not overstate, the earlier Princeton employment.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 611 and Princeton administrative records.
